title: Lock-in as a decision, not an accident

videos.script: Every service in this course ties you to Google a little. This lesson is about choosing those ties instead of collecting them. {{kinds}} First, the word itself. Lock-in is not one thing. Data that is expensive to move, an API nobody else offers, a contract with a date on it. Each costs a different amount to undo. {{seams}} Then the seams. A container, a Knative description, the Functions Framework, CloudEvents. Code that meets Google only at those points moves with little rewriting. You will run a Cloud Run function on your laptop to prove it. {{leaving}} Then the price of leaving, in three parts. Egress has a price list, and a short program reads it. Rewriting and running two systems at once are paid in weeks. {{deciding}} Last, the habit that turns all of it into a decision. One line per dependency, with the condition for looking at it again.
